findings.title: All-clients permissions ignored once any per-client resource exists
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates the schema-level "Clients" resource only when resourceStore.findByName finds no resource named with that client's internal id. As soon as any object-level permission has created that resource, the method evaluates only the object resource and never loads all-clients policies. Those policies are stored on the separate "Clients" resource, and evaluatePermission is invoked with a ResourcePermission for only one resource, so they are not applied implicitly. Consequence: a manage/view/map-roles grant on all clients stops applying to a client as soon as anyone has any object-level permission on it (even a different scope or a different user). For example, an admin with manage-all loses manage, configure, and view on client X after another user is granted view on X. The same helper backs canManage, canConfigure, canView, canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles, and the new javadoc says those checks must also honor the all-clients scope. PermissionClientTest never combines an all-clients permission with an object-level permission on the same client, so this is untested.

findings.title: Map-roles checks ignore manage-clients and cross-realm admins
findings.body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission. Unlike canManage(ClientModel) in the same class, they never short-circuit on root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS). hasPermission then returns false immediately when root.isAdminSameRealm() is false, before any policy evaluation. ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 makes AdminPermissions.evaluator/management always return MgmtPermissionsV2, so this class handles every admin request while the feature is on. Realm-management users who only have manage-clients, and master-realm admins managing another realm, are therefore denied mapping that client's roles, adding composite client roles, and mapping client-scope roles unless a fine-grained policy also exists. Those are ordinary admin operations. Callers that enforce these methods directly (requireMapRoles / requireMapCompositeRoles / requireMapClientScopeRoles) will return 403. The new tests only use myadmin, who has no manage-clients role, so the regression is not covered.

findings.title: canExchangeTo throws instead of returning a decision
findings.body: canExchangeTo unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. Token exchange decides whether the calling client may exchange for another client by invoking clients().canExchangeTo, and AdminPermissions.management returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, including for realms that have not turned on the new admin-permissions schema. The permission check therefore aborts the grant with an exception (typically a 500) instead of the boolean V1 returned. getEvaluationContext is implemented and unused, so the previous evaluation path was not wired up. A permission-check method must return false or delegate to super.canExchangeTo; it must not throw.

findings.title: Client removal still calls V2 setPermissionsEnabled, which throws
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource, and the Policy accessors all throw UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). This PR overrides MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() to return that class, and AdminPermissions.management prefers V2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. The removal listener still calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on ClientRemovedEvent when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is also enabled (the new guard only checks the V1 feature). Deleting a client then fails the transaction with UnsupportedOperationException instead of removing the client. If only V2 is enabled, the guard skips the listener and nothing deletes the per-client authorization resources this PR creates on the admin-permissions client (named by client id). Deleted clients leave orphaned resources and policies behind. setPermissionsEnabled should be a no-op under V2, and client removal should delete those V2 resources explicitly.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission does not return client ids
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission is the allowlist API callers use to filter clients by scope. It adds resource.getName() for every type "Clients" resource whose evaluation grants the scope. The schema-level resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init is named "Clients", so an all-clients grant inserts the literal string "Clients" rather than every client id. Callers comparing the set to client.getId() or client.getClientId() will not treat that as access to all clients, and a clientId of "Clients" could be confused with the type resource. Object-level resources are named with the internal client id (resolveClient returns client.getId()), which already differs from V1, where this method returned clientId strings. In addition, AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (line 104) creates those resources with create/updateScopes and never setType, so findByType(CLIENTS) will not see them unless some other layer sets the type. Object-level grants are then omitted entirely. The method cannot be used to build a correct client allowlist.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never gain Clients scopes
findings.body: init returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already non-null. Scopes and type-level resources are created only on that path, from SCHEMA. This change adds the Clients resource type and the configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes, but does not reconcile a client that was initialized when the schema contained only Users. On those realms the Clients resource and new scopes are never created. Creating a client permission then fails in getScope with ModelValidationException ("Scope [configure] does not exist") or in getOrCreateResource with ModelException ("No scopes found") when a required scope row is missing. Fresh enables work; any realm that already turned admin permissions on does not.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve client resources
findings.body: getResourceName special-cases Users: the type resource becomes "All users" and an object resource is resolved from the user id stored in resource.getName() to a username. There is no Clients branch. Client object resources are created with the internal client id as the name and no display name (getOrCreateResource only sets name, owner, and scopes). For a Clients policy the method falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null, instead of "All clients" or the clientId. Permission APIs that show which resource a policy applies to will return a null name for every client permission, and any caller that assumes a non-null display string can NPE. A missing client should be handled the same way a missing user is (ModelIllegalStateException), not silently omitted.

findings.title: Missing Clients type resource NPEs the permission check
findings.body: When no per-client resource exists, hasPermission loads the type resource and immediately calls PolicyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later resource.getScopes() with no null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null if the Clients resource was never created (init bails out when the admin-permissions client already exists) or if supportsAuthorizationSchema is false. findByResource dereferences resource.getId() and the permission check throws NullPointerException instead of returning false. An admin API call that should be denied becomes a 500. The same null resource is then passed to ResourcePermission if the isEmpty check were skipped.

findings.title: requireView javadoc describes a boolean return
findings.body: The javadoc added on requireView says it "Returns true if canView() returns true", and requireViewClientScopes says it "Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true". Both methods are void. They throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding can* check is false; they do not return a boolean. The comments document the wrong contract for every implementor of ClientPermissionEvaluator.
